comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a robot-axis damper by adjusting, locking, and physically cycling it; pr-1990 restores a gas burner by orienting and seating a burner head around an igniter, then nesting and centering its cap.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key insertion, captive-set-screw loosening/re-engagement, collar rotation, counterholding, torque-limited locking, and iterative response evaluation. pr-1990 requires pick-and-place, visual rotational alignment, compliant lowering around an obstruction, and sequential nested seating of two loose parts.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe repeatable impacts without exceeding 12 mm stroke, striking the hard stop, overloading, rebounding excessively, or drifting after locking. pr-1990 requires specified head/cap tilt, centering, height, and slot-angle tolerances, release and rest, with a penalty for dropping or throwing. Both available versions provide these pose and safety thresholds; they do not test adjustment retention or dynamic stopping.
comparison.reason: Fine rotation and alignment occur in both, but they serve different tested abilities: closed-loop damper tuning with a retained mechanical setting versus one-pass orientation and gravity seating of nested burner components.
